# jochwacht-sbom 0.12.3 — your own older bills count as yours again

If `sbom.cdx.json` already exists, the tool overwrites it only when it
wrote the file itself; anything else is left untouched. The rename dropped
`embtrace-sbom` from the list of names we have signed our output with, so
every bill written by 0.9.0 – 0.11.1 was suddenly treated as a stranger's:

```
sbom.cdx.json exists and was not written by jochwacht-sbom — it is left
untouched. Write the bill elsewhere with --sbom PATH.
```

All three names we have ever stamped are back, and a test pins them: a
stamp records the past and must not move with a rename.

Unchanged, and correct: a file written by the **embtrace suite** is still
left alone. The free collector has never overwritten one.

### If you installed the old package with pipx

`pipx` will not replace a command that another installation already owns.
If you see *"File exists at …/embtrace-sbom … Not modifying"*, the old
packages are still there:

```
pipx uninstall embtrace-sbom
pipx uninstall embtrace-check
pipx install --force jochwacht-sbom
```

One package provides all three commands; the old ones are redundant.
